title: Claude Interface Tour
description: Navigate the Claude web interface and mobile app with confidence — sidebar, conversations, projects, and settings explained.

data.text: When you log in to Claude at claude.ai, you are greeted with a clean, minimal interface designed to keep the focus on your conversation. The layout is intentionally simple: a sidebar on the left for navigation and your conversation history, a large central area for the chat, and a text input at the bottom.

data.title: Elements you need to know:
items: Sidebar — shows your conversation history, projects, and settings. Click the hamburger menu to collapse it.
New chat button — starts a fresh conversation. Each chat is independent unless you use Projects.
Input area — where you type your messages. Supports Shift+Enter for new lines.
Model selector — choose between Claude Sonnet, Opus, or Haiku depending on your needs.
Artifact panel — appears when Claude generates an artifact (code, document, visualization).

data.text: Claude organizes your work into two structures: conversations and projects. A conversation is a single chat thread — start a new one when you switch to a different topic. A project is a collection of related conversations that share a common context, files, and instructions. Projects are powerful for ongoing work like writing a book, building a product, or managing a research topic.

data.title: Screenshot description
data.content: Screenshot of Claude interface showing the sidebar with conversation history, the main chat area with a conversation about data analysis, and the artifact panel on the right showing generated Python code.

data.text: Claude accepts a wide range of file types: PDFs, Word documents, text files, spreadsheets, images, and code files. Click the paperclip icon in the input area to upload. Once uploaded, Claude can read, analyze, summarize, and answer questions about the content. This is one of Claude's most powerful features — you can effectively 'hand' Claude a book and ask it to explain specific chapters.

The Claude mobile app (iOS and Android) provides a similar experience to the web interface. The main difference is the layout is optimized for smaller screens, and voice input is available as an alternative to typing. Conversations sync across devices, so you can start on your phone and continue on desktop.

data.title: Pro tip for desktop users
data.text: Use keyboard shortcuts to navigate faster: Ctrl/Cmd + N for new chat, Ctrl/Cmd + / to focus the input, and Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + C to copy the last response. Check Settings > Keyboard shortcuts for the full list.

data.title: Interface essentials
points: Projects group related chats with shared context and files
Upload files via the paperclip icon — PDFs, docs, images, and code
Choose between Sonnet (balanced), Opus (powerful), or Haiku (fast)
Mobile app syncs conversations across devices
